Meta.title: AFA · Business process automation
Meta.description: AFA hands your business's repetitive work to a system: customer replies, order capture, follow-up and reporting. The decisions that matter stay yours.

Hero.sub: From before the first visit to after the sale.

Map.hubNote: No process on this map runs without a human checkpoint. That is a design constraint, not a setting.
Map.figureLabel: The AFA operating map: six domains, twenty-four automatable processes

sales.title: Sales
sales.summary: From a stranger's first message to the deal landing with a named person.

operations.title: Operations
operations.summary: Everything after the order is taken; the part that usually lives in someone's head.

intelligence.title: Reporting
intelligence.summary: Turning what got recorded into something a decision can rest on.

finance.title: Finance
finance.summary: Where money comes in, where it gets stuck, and when to chase it.

support.title: Support
support.summary: Every request that arrives after the sale, until it is closed.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.summary: Getting the right message to someone who has bought from you before.

lead-capture.title: Lead capture
lead-capture.trigger: A message on WhatsApp, Instagram, the site form, or a missed call.
lead-capture.decision: New customer or returning? Which product are they asking about?
lead-capture.action: One record is created with the channel, the message and the time. Nothing is retyped.
lead-capture.human: An unclear source is checked with you before it is assigned.

quote.title: Quote
quote.trigger: A lead with a product and a quantity.
quote.decision: Price, discount and validity read from your own rules.
quote.action: A numbered quote goes out in the same conversation.
quote.human: Any discount past your ceiling reaches you before it goes out.

deal-followup.title: Stalled-deal follow-up
deal-followup.trigger: A deal sitting in one stage longer than you allow.
deal-followup.action: One short nudge on the same channel. Twice at most, then it stops.
deal-followup.human: Muting follow-up for any customer is one click.

handoff.title: Rep handoff
handoff.trigger: A lead that has become serious.
handoff.decision: Which rep, by current load and territory, not turn-taking.
handoff.action: The whole conversation moves with the file; the customer never repeats themselves.
handoff.human: Handoff is reversible and every change is recorded.

order-intake.title: Order intake
order-intake.trigger: A confirmed order from any channel.
order-intake.decision: Are the items, address and payment complete?
order-intake.action: The order joins one queue, with an id, where everyone can see it.
order-intake.human: An incomplete order is not rejected; it waits for you in review.

stock-check.title: Stock check
stock-check.trigger: Every new order, plus one daily sweep.
stock-check.decision: Real stock minus what has been promised; not just the warehouse number.
stock-check.action: A line running low is reported to purchasing before it hits zero.
stock-check.human: A purchase order is never raised automatically. Only proposed.

dispatch.title: Dispatch scheduling
dispatch.trigger: An order or job that is ready to go.
dispatch.decision: Who, where, and with how much capacity left today?
dispatch.action: The slot reaches the customer and the technician, in both calendars.

sla-watch.title: Response-time watch
sla-watch.decision: How long to the promised deadline, holidays counted?
sla-watch.action: A case at risk surfaces before it is late, not after.
sla-watch.human: You set the deadlines; the system just guards them.

daily-brief.title: Daily brief
daily-brief.trigger: One fixed hour, every working day.
daily-brief.action: A short summary lands where the team already reads.
daily-brief.human: You define what it covers and who gets it.

anomaly.title: Deviation alert
anomaly.trigger: Any number the system tracks continuously.
anomaly.decision: Is this normal for this weekday, this season?
anomaly.action: The odd one out is reported with context: what, how far, since when.
anomaly.human: Nothing is auto-corrected. You get the news; you decide.

forecast.title: Demand forecast
forecast.trigger: The close of any period you define.
forecast.decision: Past trend, season and calendar events read together.
forecast.action: A range with its margin of error; never one confident number.
forecast.human: Every forecast is labelled an estimate, source data in view.

board-pack.title: Management pack
board-pack.trigger: Month end, or whatever period you run.
board-pack.decision: Which handful of numbers matter this period?
board-pack.action: A presentable document, every figure traceable.
board-pack.human: It reaches you before anyone else.

invoice.title: Invoice issue
invoice.trigger: An order delivered or a job done.
invoice.decision: Tax, discount and terms per the contract.
invoice.action: Numbered, sent, and written to the books.
invoice.human: An unusual invoice is approved before it leaves.

reconcile.title: Payment matching
reconcile.decision: Which open invoice do the amount, date and reference fit?
reconcile.action: Matches settle; misfits wait on a review list rather than being forced.
reconcile.human: No financial record closes without a definite match.

dunning.title: Receivables follow-up
dunning.trigger: An invoice past its due date.
dunning.decision: What tone, what interval? This customer's history says.
dunning.action: Reminders step up gradually; every reply sticks to the file.
dunning.human: One word from you stops it; anything serious reaches you first.

payout.title: Supplier payout
payout.decision: Do the purchase order, goods receipt and invoice agree?
payout.action: The payment queues with all its paperwork attached.
payout.human: A payment never executes on its own. Final approval always rests with a person.

triage.title: Ticket triage
triage.decision: What is it, how urgent, do we have an approved answer?
triage.action: The request enters the right queue, tagged and prioritised.
triage.human: A wrong call is fixed in one click, and the system learns.

first-reply.title: First reply
first-reply.trigger: A request whose subject is known.
first-reply.decision: The answer comes from your approved material, not thin air.
first-reply.action: Sent on the same channel, any hour of the day.
first-reply.human: An answer the system is unsure of is not sent at all.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.trigger: A request the automatic answer did not solve, or a sensitive one.
escalation.decision: Which specialist, by subject and who is actually there.
escalation.action: The full history moves along; the customer never retells the story.
escalation.human: The customer is informed their case has reached a specialist.

csat.title: Post-resolution survey
csat.decision: Only genuinely resolved cases are asked.
csat.action: One short question; the answer sticks to the case.
csat.human: A low score reaches you that moment, not month-end.

segment.title: Customer segments
segment.trigger: Any change in buying behaviour or status.
segment.decision: Groups computed from real behaviour, not a hand-kept list.
segment.action: Segments stay current, ready for any campaign.
segment.human: Every group can be reviewed and edited before use.

campaign.title: Campaign send
campaign.trigger: A scheduled slot, or an event like a birthday or repeat purchase.
campaign.decision: How many messages has this person had lately? Nobody gets worn out.
campaign.action: Sent on the channel that person actually answers.
campaign.human: No campaign reaches a list without your approval.

content-queue.title: Publishing queue
content-queue.decision: The best hour, from when your audience is really active.
content-queue.action: Published to the set channels; each post's result recorded.
content-queue.human: Writing and sign-off stay yours; the system only publishes.

attribution.title: Channel results
attribution.trigger: Any sale whose path can be traced.
attribution.decision: Credit follows the customer's real journey, not the last click.
attribution.action: Cost and result per channel, side by side.
attribution.human: A channel without enough data reads unknown, never zero.

Manifesto.statement: Systems do the repetitive work; people make the decisions.

human.title: You decide
human.body: Nothing important happens without your sign-off.

ownership.title: Your ownership
ownership.body: Code, domain and data are registered in your name from day one.

auditable.title: Your own dashboard
auditable.body: Everything the system does is logged and visible in a panel built for you.

reversible.title: Easy to deactivate
reversible.body: Any part can be deactivated without stopping the work.

restaurant.title: Every order in one queue
restaurant.before: Orders came by phone, Instagram and WhatsApp and went onto paper. On busy nights, messages got lost.
restaurant.after: Every order from every channel records itself, and the kitchen and the till watch one list.

retail.title: From DMs to a real online store
retail.before: Every sale took a thread of messages, and after the sale no customer record survived.
retail.after: Catalogue and payment moved online; recurring questions answer themselves and every purchase lands in the customer's file.

services.title: Dispatch without the notebook
services.before: Requests were taken by phone and written in a notebook; follow-ups slipped.
services.after: Requests record and schedule themselves; customer and technician both get reminders.

Impact.title: How much time comes back to your team?
Impact.subtitle: Enter your business's details; the result is computed on the spot.

staff.label: How many people do repetitive work?

hours.label: How many hours each, per day?

missed.label: What share goes unanswered or unfollowed?

Impact.disclaimer: An estimate from your own inputs, not a delivery promise. It assumes roughly 60% of repetitive work can be handed to a system and roughly 70% of missed requests can be rescued; the exact figures follow a review of your processes.

timeline.q: How long until the first part is running?
timeline.a: Usually two to four weeks for one complete process, depending on how many tools need connecting. The first call gives a tighter range.

wrong.q: What happens when it gets something wrong?
wrong.a: Every process has a human checkpoint and everything the system does is recorded. A mistake is either stopped before it runs, or traceable and reversible after.

data.a: On infrastructure registered to your own company. We hold access only as long as you want us to, and removing it is simple admin.

tools.q: Do we have to replace our current tools?
tools.a: No. We start by connecting the tools you already use. A swap is only suggested when the tool itself is the obstacle.

pricing.a: After the review call, based on how many processes and tools are involved. Any number before that is a guess.

exit.q: What if we stop working together?
exit.a: The system keeps running; the code and access were yours from the start. We hand over the docs and nothing stays tied to us.
